## Summary

`autodeploy.sh` keeps ONE piece of global state for TWO independently-deploying components (the
review-bot and the mcp blue-green target). Split out of `cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95` with the
operator's approval: that ticket scopes the review-bot DEFERRAL so control reaches the mcp
block; this one makes the state each component depends on per-component.

Four rounds of code review on the combined change each found the same defect shape, each fix
exposing the next. They are one concern and belong in one ticket.

## The three couplings

**Completion.** `deployed-sha` is written once, at the footer, so ANY early exit loses the
completion of whichever component DID deploy, and the next tick redeploys it. A review-bot
redeploy stop-and-drains the container, killing an in-flight review (bug 34cd) — the exact
harm the drain gate exists to prevent, arriving from the other direction.

**Failure.** `record_backoff_failure` writes ONE `deploy-backoff` keyed on the global `$TARGET`,
and the top-level gate exits the whole script on it. On `main` it is called from BOTH blocks
(~5 sites in the bot block, ~10 in the mcp block), so an mcp failure throttles the BOT and a
bot failure suppresses mcp.

**Incompleteness.** A component skipped by an open backoff window has not deployed, but nothing
records that, so the footer stamps `$TARGET` into its marker for a deploy that never ran. The
next tick then computes no delta and drops the pending change PERMANENTLY.

## Shape of the fix

- `mcp-deployed-sha` and `bot-deployed-sha`, each written the moment that component completes,
  with each component's delta gate RE-POINTED to diff from its own marker rather than the
  global `$DEPLOYED` baseline. An absent or unparseable marker falls back to `$DEPLOYED`.
  The global `deployed-sha` KEEPS its existing role unchanged: it is the TICK-level record,
  advanced only at the footer and only on a tick that completed, and it still drives the
  top-level "up to date; no-op" early exit (`if [ "$TARGET" = "$DEPLOYED" ]`). It is not
  removed and not split — the component markers are added ALONGSIDE it. On a complete tick the
  footer ALSO stamps both component markers. Those two writes are not in conflict: the
  mid-tick write records a component that actually DEPLOYED, and the footer write is an
  idempotent top-up covering the component that was a NO-OP this tick (nothing changed under
  its trigger paths), so it is never left behind the global marker. For a component that
  already deployed, the footer rewrites the same value. On an INCOMPLETE tick the guard exits
  before the footer, so the only markers written are the mid-tick ones for components that
  genuinely deployed — which is precisely the asymmetry per-component state exists to record. `$DEPLOYED` also remains the fallback baseline for a component whose marker is
  absent or unparseable, which is what makes the first tick after upgrade behave as today.

- A separate `mcp-deploy-backoff` recorder; the existing file then records bot failures only,
  which is what makes it safe to move its gate off the top of the script. Each gate sits with
  the component it throttles and skips that component instead of exiting the tick.
- `bot_incomplete` / `mcp_incomplete`, honoured by the footer guard, so a backoff-skip with a
  delta still pending never records completion. Each gate tests the DELTA before the window, so
  "nothing to do" stays distinguishable from "skipped with work pending".
- Both recorders keep emitting the `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker. That token — not the reason
  string — is what the alarm counts: `infra/scripts/observability.sh:230` does a bare
  `grep -cE '^AUTODEPLOY_ERROR \{'` over the unit journal and publishes the count as
  `rebar/host:deploy_errors` (`:240`, §4d). It never parses the reason, so alarm continuity is
  preserved by continuing to emit the marker at all. The reason stays `deploy_failed` and
  gains a `component=mcp` marker for OPERATOR legibility — telling the two paths apart when
  reading the journal — not for the metric.

## Consumers outside autodeploy.sh

The marker's only non-test consumer is `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (§4d, lines 230/240),
which counts `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` occurrences into `rebar/host:deploy_errors`. It is deliberately
kept distinct from the deferral and retire-cap tokens (`:259-260`, `:282`, `:338`) so routine
deferrals and retire-caps never inflate that alarm — this change adds no new token, so that
separation is unchanged. Test consumers of the marker: `test_autodeploy_review_drain.py`,
`test_autodeploy_health_gate.py`, `test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py`,
`test_observability_marker_anchor_8c2f.py`.

The one test consumer of the shared STATE FILE is `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py:86`,
which reads `state/deploy-backoff` after a REVIEW-BOT failure. That file keeps its name and
keeps recording bot failures, so the test needs no change and continues to pass unmodified —
verified, 4 passed. Only the mcp block's failures move to the new file, and no existing test
reads that path. Had the split renamed `deploy-backoff` instead of narrowing what writes to it,
this consumer would have broken silently; narrowing rather than renaming is what avoids that.

## Boundary correction (2026-08-27)

The mcp completion marker (`mcp-deployed-sha` and re-pointing the mcp delta gate to it) has
MOVED to `cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95`. Code review showed the original boundary was wrong: without
that marker, cf34's fix re-triggers a full blue-green cutover on every tick of a deferral
episode, so making the mcp path REACHABLE on a deferred tick and keeping it from redeploying
every deferred tick are one concern and belong in one change. This ticket keeps the BOT-side
marker, the scoped backoffs, and the incompleteness flags.

## Deliberately out of scope

A bot FATAL path still exits the tick, so mcp misses that single tick, after which the bot is in
backoff and skipped and mcp proceeds. Bounding it to one tick is enough; making the bot's fatal
paths return rather than exit is a larger restructure of a live deploy script.

## Acceptance criteria

All six mutation-checked: removing the behaviour each guards returns its test to RED.

- [x] An mcp failure does not write the SHARED backoff.
      Proof: `test_mcp_failure_on_a_deferred_tick_does_not_backoff_the_bot`
- [x] An mcp failure does not cause the review-bot to redeploy on later ticks.
      Proof: `test_a_failed_mcp_deploy_does_not_redeploy_the_bot_every_tick`
- [x] A component skipped by its own backoff window is not recorded as deployed (both halves).
      Proof: `test_bot_backoff_tick_does_not_record_the_bot_as_deployed`,
      `test_mcp_backoff_tick_does_not_record_mcp_as_deployed`
- [x] An open backoff window with NO pending delta is not reported as a skip.
      Proof: `test_an_open_bot_backoff_with_no_pending_delta_is_not_reported_as_a_skip`
- [x] An mcp backoff throttles mcp while the review-bot still deploys on the same tick.
      Proof: `test_mcp_backoff_throttles_only_mcp_and_lets_the_bot_deploy` — mutating the mcp
      recorder to also poison the shared backoff kills it on the bot assertion specifically.
- [x] mcp failures still emit an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker, so `deploy_errors`
      (`observability.sh:230,240`) counts them as before, and the reason names `component=mcp`.
      Proof: `test_mcp_failure_keeps_the_deploy_failed_metric_and_names_the_component`


## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/ -q -p no:randomly

Each new test is mutation-checked: removing the behaviour it guards returns it to RED.
